sheets.title: IV Fluids & Tonicity
sheets.summary: Which fluid moves where — and when to use each.

rows.note: Fluid resuscitation, blood loss, dehydration; only fluid with blood.
Surgery, burns; contains K⁺ — avoid in renal failure/hyperkalemia.
Becomes hypotonic once glucose is metabolized.
Can cause cerebral edema — avoid with increased ICP or head injury.
Risk of fluid overload — give slowly, monitor lungs and sodium.

sheets.pearl: Iso stays, Hypo swells the cell, Hyper shrinks the cell. Never give hypotonic fluids with increased ICP.

sheets.title: Thyroid: Hypo vs Hyper
sheets.summary: Everything slows down vs. everything speeds up.

rows.v: Fatigue, weight gain, cold intolerance, bradycardia, constipation
Weight loss, heat intolerance, tachycardia, diarrhea, anxiety

sheets.pearl: Hypo = slow, cold, gain. Hyper = fast, hot, lose. Thyroid storm and myxedema coma are the emergencies.

sheets.title: Adrenal: Cushing's vs Addison's
sheets.summary: Too much cortisol vs. too little — mirror images.

rows.v: Moon face, buffalo hump, truncal obesity, striae
High glucose, high sodium, LOW potassium, hypertension
Low glucose, LOW sodium, HIGH potassium, hypotension
rows.note: Addisonian crisis: give IV steroids + saline.

sheets.pearl: Cushing's = Cushioned/excess (high everything but K⁺). Addison's = Absent (low everything but K⁺). Never stop steroids abruptly.

sheets.title: Immunizations & Live Vaccine Cautions
sheets.summary: The schedule highlights and who must avoid live vaccines.

rows.v: MMR, varicella, rotavirus, intranasal flu, yellow fever

rows.note: Can cause disease in these groups.

sheets.pearl: Hold vaccines for moderate/severe illness (a mild cold is fine). Live vaccines: not in pregnancy or immunocompromise.

sheets.title: Toxicities & Overdose Signs
sheets.summary: Recognize the poisoning — and its antidote.

rows.v: Hot, dry, red, delirious, dilated pupils
rows.note: “Mad as a hatter, dry as a bone.”

rows.v: SLUDGE: salivation, lacrimation, urination, defecation, GI, emesis

rows.note: Give 100% oxygen; pulse ox reads falsely normal.

sheets.pearl: If a stem gives a classic toxidrome + a drug level, the answer is stop exposure and give the specific antidote.

sheets.title: Wound Care & Surgical Drains
sheets.summary: Drain types, healing, and dressing choices.

rows.note: Compress the bulb to re-establish suction.
Drains onto a dressing; secured with a safety pin.

rows.v: Open wound heals from the base up

rows.note: Being phased out for gentler options.
Match the dressing to the drainage.

sheets.pearl: Empty and measure closed drains; report a sudden increase or a change to bright-red bleeding.

sheets.title: Preeclampsia & Maternal Danger Signs
sheets.summary: The hypertensive disorders of pregnancy and when to act.

rows.note: Severe features: BP ≥160/110, headache, visual changes, RUQ pain.

rows.v: Hemolysis, Elevated Liver enzymes, Low Platelets

rows.note: Toxicity: lost reflexes, RR <12, low urine output.

rows.v: Severe headache, visual changes, epigastric/RUQ pain, ↓fetal movement, bleeding
rows.note: Teach the client to call immediately.

sheets.pearl: Preeclampsia teaching: report headache, visual changes, and epigastric pain — these signal worsening/seizure risk.

sheets.title: Mental Health Medication Classes
sheets.summary: The psych drug classes and their signature warnings.
sheets.pearl: MAOIs + tyramine = hypertensive crisis. Clozapine = watch WBC (agranulocytosis). SSRIs take weeks.

sheets.title: Pain Management
sheets.summary: Assessing and treating pain across ages.

rows.note: Pain is what the client says it is.

sheets.pearl: Pain is subjective — believe the client's report. Assess respiratory rate BEFORE giving an opioid.

sheets.title: Respiratory Conditions Compared
sheets.summary: Telling the common respiratory problems apart.

rows.v: Sudden dyspnea, pleuritic pain, tachycardia, hypoxia
Absent breath sounds; tension → tracheal deviation
rows.note: Chest tube; tension = emergency needle decompression.

sheets.pearl: COPD → keep SpO₂ 88–92% (don't over-oxygenate). Sudden dyspnea + pleuritic chest pain + tachycardia → think PE.

sheets.title: Seizure Care & Precautions
sheets.summary: What to do during a seizure and how to keep the client safe.

rows.v: Ease to the floor, side-lying, protect the head
rows.note: Turn to the side to prevent aspiration.

rows.v: Put anything in the mouth or restrain the client
Time it, note the activity, stay with the client
Padded rails, bed low, suction/O₂ at bedside, IV access
Seizure >5 min or repeated without recovery

sheets.pearl: During a seizure: side-lying, protect the head, time it — never restrain or put anything in the mouth.

sheets.title: Anticoagulants & Antiplatelets
sheets.summary: Monitoring and reversal for the blood thinners.

rows.note: Antidote: vitamin K; keep vitamin-K foods consistent.
Don't expel the air bubble; rotate sites.
Bleeding risk; hold before some procedures.

sheets.pearl: Heparin = aPTT + protamine. Warfarin = INR + vitamin K. All: bleeding precautions (soft brush, no IM, fall safety).
